data.title: Oil producer NABEP to increase Venezuela fleet to 41 rigs in November
data.description:
Oil producer North America Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) said on Saturday it will increase its in-country fleet in Venezuela to 41 rigs in November.

Earlier this month, the company announced it planned to deploy 60 rigs in the South American country.

The company's production reached 223,509 barrels of oil equivalent per day in October, up from about 200,000 boepd in August, as the buildout continues.

  • Nine drilling rigs are in Venezuela: three are active in the Junin 10 block of the Orinoco Belt, three more will start there soon, and three are being refurbished or moved.

  • Four more drilling rigs are being shipped from Houston, Brazil and Colombia.

  • The company has 20 workover rigs in Venezuela: three in Lake Maracaibo, 12 in the Lagunillas and Bachaquero fields and five in the Orinoco Belt.

  • Fifteen more workover rigs are being refurbished in Houston for deployment in western Venezuela.

  • The first million barrels of oil under the August 2026 agreement with the US State Department and US Defense Department arrived in Corpus Christi, Texas, on October 27, NABEP said.

  • "We are paying for every one of these rigs with the oil we produce," NABEP CEO Alejandro Betancourt said.

data.title: Bitcoin Looks Like A 'Relative Dud' Against Gold And US Treasuries, Says Bloomberg's Mike McGlone
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bloomberg Intelligence strategist Mike McGlone said one Bitcoin currently buys roughly 20 ounces of gold, predicting the ratio is more likely to fall further.
  • Bitcoin is also underperforming long-term U.S. Treasuries. McGlone said the IBIT-to-TLT ratio stood at 81 as of Friday.
  • McGlone warned that Bitcoin's continued weakness below $80,000 could signal broader pressure on risk assets.

Bitcoin (BTC) is losing ground to gold and long-dated U.S. Treasuries, warned Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodity strategist Mike McGlone. He added that the slide could extend into risk assets.

On X, McGlone made his case saying Bitcoin purchased roughly 20 ounces of gold on Saturday, and the ratio is more likely to fall toward 15 than to rise toward 25. He noted that early in 2021, amid a deluge of pandemic-era stimulus, the ratio first reached the 20 mark. He claimed that since then, Bitcoin has fluctuated roughly three times as much as gold while remaining stagnant.

McGlone said that record "puts Bitcoin in the category of a relative dud." He asked if the cryptocurrency could still prove that "it's not a has-been." A hold above 20 would indicate a recovery. According to McGlone, a break in either direction could have an impact on stocks as well because the ratio has closely followed the Nasdaq-100 Index.

Treasuries Pull Ahead

McGlone contrasted the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond exchange-traded fund (TLT) and BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) in a second post. At the end of 2024, he set both at 100.

He stated that on October 30, the IBIT-to-TLT ratio was 81. IBIT is roughly four times more volatile than TLT, but it hasn't been able to stay above 100 since the fourth quarter of 2025.

McGlone said that the weak run started in 2024, the same year that US spot Bitcoin funds opened and President Trump changed his mind about his views on cryptocurrencies. He said that the poor performance "may mean that Bitcoin's glory days are over."

Bitcoin's $80K Struggle Signals Risk-Asset Concerns

He said that the market for US Treasuries was one of the world's most leveraged. Having bonds do better than Bitcoin for about two years, he said, could show what's to come if Bitcoin stays below $80,000.

Bitcoin’s price on Saturday was around $77,300, which is 3.4% less than the level that McGlone pointed out. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

Additionally, Visser said that Bitcoin's muted response to the Binance (BNB) hack showed that the price has "been lower than AI names all year." He said that over the last six weeks, Bitcoin had mostly moved in sync with semiconductor stocks. Now, he said that the U.S. Treasury's announcement next week about refinancing could make things easier for Bitcoin, gold, and AI stocks this year.

data.title: Nifty 500 vs S&P 500: India or US, innovation is the only game in town for investors
data.description:
Foreign investors have never been this bearish on India, or so the latest market chatter goes. Just two years ago, they could hardly get enough of Indian equities. How quickly sentiment changes! Meanwhile, a section of Dalal Street apparently believes every market disappointment deserves a government remedy. But amid all the wailing, investors may be missing the forest for the trees, yet again. What if India’s bigger problem is not insufficient encouragement to buy its stocks, but a lack of innovation among the companies issuing them?

And this may not be India’s problem alone. Even in America, the stock market is increasingly distinguishing between businesses driving innovation and those struggling to keep pace.

At the headline level, the S&P 500 has been a golden goose for investors, with its 27 per cent CAGR returns (includes benefits from INR depreciation vs USD) and 16 per cent CAGR outperformance over India’s Nifty 500 in three-year period (ended October 30, 2026), when looking on an equal weight basis, its edge over India’s Nifty 500 gives a more nuanced picture.

An analysis based on equal weights weeds out the impact of few stocks with outsized returns and gives a colour on broader health of the market. On a five-year basis, there is hardly anything to choose between the two equal-weight indices with S&P 500 returns (in rupee terms) at a CAGR of 12 per cent versus Nifty 500’s CAGR of 11 per cent. On a 10-year basis too, the difference is not alarming at 14 and 12 per cent, respectively.

A closer look at the S&P 500 also reveals its share of pain points. 58 per cent of S&P 500 stocks are trading at levels 20 per cent or more below its all-time highs. Yes, that’s not as bad as the Nifty 500’s 78 per cent, but data makes it clear even in the most innovative economy investors are punishing non-AI stocks or even a few AI stocks in recent days.

US lesson

In America, established businesses have paid a price for losing their innovative edge. Nike, Netflix, Lululemon, Intel, Kraft Heinz, Dow Inc, and Ford Motor, grappling with past valuation excesses, or stale product offerings or competition from nimbler rivals, individually trade more than 50 per cent below their respective all-time highs. Put simply, innovation is no longer optional, even for celebrated brands.

Tech companies have not been spared either. Adobe, for instance, is down 64 per cent from its all-time high and 31 per cent from its 52-week high, as concerns over AI disruption weigh on its prospects. Companies unable to adapt risk losing relevance.

Excessive valuations, discussed in our page 1 article ‘When stock valuations go wrong, blame taxes?’ (October 18), explain part of the recent stock market pain. Yet they leave behind a more uncomfortable reality. Amid the global race for technological breakthroughs, the silence from India’s corporate giants is almost deafening.

Technological leadership demands more than just intent or ambition.

This is reflected in a more direct way in mutual funds marketed around innovation theme in India. Depending on the fund, top holdings included ICICI Bank, Eternal (Zomato), Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, Adani Ports, Reliance Industries, Info Edge, Trent and Varun Beverages among their largest investments. Compare these with Innovation ETFs in the US, whose holdings include Micron, Tesla, Tempus AI and Marvell Technology, businesses associated with autonomous technology, AI-driven healthcare and gene editing.

One can argue these funds have different mandates, and improvements in distribution, banking or consumer businesses certainly qualify as innovation. Yet the contrast highlights the relatively limited choice of frontier-technology companies available to domestic equity investors.

No breakthroughs

Money, meanwhile, has hardly been India’s principal constraint. For calendar 2025 (a year not impacted by war-related raw material spikes) the Nifty 500’s pre-tax profit margin of 12.8 per cent compared with 12.2 per cent for the S&P 500 excluding America’s Magnificent Seven stocks. Indian companies also enjoyed considerably higher margins than their counterparts in Germany (7.7 per cent), Japan (9.9 per cent) and the UK (11.2 per cent). Clearly, corporate India has hardly been starved of profitability cushion to back innovation.

Yet research spending tells another story. Top listed Indian IT services companies spent about ₹1,000 crore to ₹3,000 crore in R&D, or 1-2 per cent of total expenses, in FY26. Clearly, profitable businesses and a technology services workforce do not automatically produce globally dominant intellectual property without higher investments.

The government has hardly been inactive. Corporate tax cuts in 2019, manufacturing incentives and infrastructure investment sought to encourage businesses to invest. The results in breakthrough commercial innovation remain less impressive.

That is not to suggest India has never produced genuine innovators. The country has made significant strides in pharmaceuticals, automobiles, emerging technologies and digital payments, particularly UPI. Bengaluru-based Sarvam AI raised $234 million in June. Yet such companies are still largely missing from the listed universe and, consequently, have little bearing on overall stock market performance.

India cannot summon global capital merely by making its stock market friendlier. Taiwan’s semiconductors, South Korea’s memory chips and America’s AI ecosystem offer exposure to technologies the world increasingly needs. Indian companies must build more such globally indispensable businesses. Fund managers lobbying for LTCG tax cuts should also push for more innovation from their portfolio stocks. Otherwise, investors may continue debating the cost of owning Indian stocks while overlooking the more consequential question: what do these companies actually own?

data.title: IHCL and Ambuja Neotia open AltAir House – IHCL SeleQtions in Kolkata and Siliguri
data.description:
Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL) and Ambuja Neotia have announced the opening of AltAir House – IHCL SeleQtions in Kolkata and Siliguri. The announcement also marks a strengthening of the companies' partnership, with Ambuja Neotia committing Rs 2,700 crore towards West Bengal's hospitality sector across IHCL's brand portfolio in Kolkata, Raichak, Digha, Siliguri, Lataguri, Kalimpong and Darjeeling.

The investment includes the two newly opened hotels and a Rs 100 crore expansion of Taj Chia Kutir Resort & Spa, Darjeeling, which will add 28 keys and 15,000 sq ft of banqueting facilities.

Puneet Chhatwal, Managing Director and CEO, IHCL, said, “Our longstanding partnership with Ambuja Neotia strengthens with the opening of AltAir House under the IHCL SeleQtions brand in Kolkata and Siliguri. AltAir House, with its bespoke design and experiences, is an ideal fit for the IHCL SeleQtions platform. Launched under a franchise arrangement, these openings mark a new chapter in our journey.”

He added, “Rooted in a shared vision, IHCL and Ambuja Neotia are committed to advancing tourism, creating new travel experiences, and expanding the presence of IHCL’s brands across the region.”

Harshavardhan Neotia, Chairman, Ambuja Neotia Group, said, “Bengal offers an extraordinary diversity of landscapes and cultural experiences, from its vibrant cities and riverfronts to its forests, tea gardens and the Himalayas. Our investment commitment of about Rs 2,700 crore reflects our confidence in the region’s tourism potential and our aspiration to create destinations that people will want to experience and revisit.”

He added, “Our association with IHCL has grown over the years through a shared appreciation for thoughtful hospitality. With the launch of AltAir House – IHCL SeleQtions, we aim to create a more individual expression with every hotel telling its own design story, offering distinctive dining experiences and inviting spaces for people to come together. Alongside the continued growth of our Kutir series with IHCL, this marks an important milestone in our partnership.”

Building on the legacy of AltAir in Salt Lake Sector V, Kolkata, a destination for hospitality, dining and leisure for nearly a decade, AltAir House – IHCL SeleQtions debuts as a design-led boutique hospitality offering. Each property is envisioned to tell its own story through architecture, art and design, complemented by curated culinary experiences, signature dining concepts and spaces for gatherings and celebrations.

Located at Ecospace Business Park, New Town, AltAir House – IHCL SeleQtions, Kolkata, features 42 individually designed rooms and suites inspired by Bengal's cultural heritage. The hotel also offers art-led interiors, curated dining and lounge experiences, wellness facilities and spaces for celebrations. The Siliguri property, located within Uttorayon Township, offers 60 rooms and suites inspired by the region's cultural diversity, along with curated dining and indoor and outdoor event spaces that can accommodate up to 1,200 guests.

IHCL and Ambuja Neotia's upcoming projects in West Bengal include Taj Ananta Kutir and Taj Uvanta Signature Residences in Kolkata; Taj Himya Kutir and Taj Himya Branded Villas in Darjeeling; Taj Terai Kutir in Siliguri; Taj Vanya Kutir in Lataguri; AltAir House – IHCL SeleQtions properties in Raichak, Kalimpong, Digha and Lataguri; and Tree of Life in Siliguri.

The partnership currently comprises a portfolio of over 80 properties across India, including 55 resorts under Tree of Life, IHCL's experiential leisure brand.

data.title: Jio Platforms up 27.8% since IPO listing but how RIL, Jio Fin, Alok Ind, Network 18, Lotus shares fared in 3 years?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- The much awaited initial public offering (IPO), Jio Platforms, made a spectacular stock market debut this week, with shares listing at a nearly 21.26% premium over the issue price. Backed by Reliance Industries Limited, Jio shares have surged 27.8% over the IPO price.

While Jio Platforms shares are stealing the spotlight, here's a look at how other stocks from Mukesh Ambani's Reliance group have performed over the past three years.

The Reliance Group's listed companies include Reliance Industries Limited, Jio Financial Services, Alok Industries, Network18 Media and Lotus Chocolate Company.

RIL share price closed 0.44% lower at Rs.1163.55 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.15,74,578.54 crore on Friday, October 30. The stock has declined 21.83% in one year, 13.42% in two years. Its share price value has surged merely 0.68% in three years.

Shares of Jio Financial Services closed 1.21% lower at Rs.204.50 per share on BSE with an MCap of Rs.1,35,034.25 crore on Friday. The stock has declined 5.59% in one month, 17.17% in three months and around 30.82% in 2026 so far (YTD).

Alok Industries stock closed 5.49% lower at Rs.8.09 per share on BSE with an MCap of Rs.4,016.88 crore. The textile stock has declined 53.85% in one year. RIL holds 40.01% stake in the textile stock.

Shares of Network 18 Media & Investments Limited closed 1.86% lower at Rs.23.68 per share on BSE with an MCap of Rs.3,651.46 crore on BSE on Friday. Its share price value has declined 51.08% in one year, 70.84% in two years, and 65.78% in three years.

Lotus Chocolate Company's share price closed 508.40 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.652.84 crore on Friday. Its share price value has declined 64.41% in two years, but has surged 88% in three years.

data.title: African lenders formally establish $5 billion energy bank
data.description:
The African Export-Import Bank and the African Petroleum Producers' Organisation have formally established the Africa Energy Bank, according to a statement from Afreximbank on Saturday.

The bank, which has authorised capital of $5 billion, aims to bridge a financing gap as traditional lenders withdraw funding from fossil fuels, even as oil and gas remain central to Africa's energy systems.

  • The bank's inaugural general meeting, held in Abuja, Nigeria, appointed Helmy Ghazi as its first president and formed its first board of directors

  • The continent's energy investment needs are estimated at $200 billion, according to the announcement

  • The bank will support projects across the energy value chain, including exploration and production, refining and distribution

  • Reuters reported in February 2025 that the bank was targeting a mid-year 2025 launch, with South Africa indicating interest in joining despite not being an APPO member

  • The bank would target an asset base of $120 billion, Reuters reported earlier

data.title: Binance restores 90% of stolen crypto assets
data.description:
Binance said on Saturday that it has covered 90% of cryptocurrency assets affected by a massive cyberattack this week, and the company remains on track to resume withdrawals by Sunday within its previously stated timeline.

In a statement on X, the world’s largest crypto exchange said that the remaining 10% of the stolen assets consist of less liquid tokens, which means that the time it takes to replenish them will be longer.

Binance initiated the recoveries after disclosing on Friday that a security incident impacted about $6.3B of client assets, which it said will be fully covered using its own funds and its Secure Asset Fund for Users established in 2018.

Shares of crypto exchange Coinbase Global and Bitcoin buyer Strategy fell after the announcement, and several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group , froze funds linked to the hack.

“We will continue to buy the remaining relevant token assets through market and OTC channels until the covered amount reaches 100% for all tokens," Binance said. "Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.”

Fully recovered assets include Bitcoin USD , Ethereum USD , Tether USD (USDT-USD), Binance Coin USD (BNB-USD), Solana USD , USDC , Ripple USD , and ZCash USD (ZEC-USD).

Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

data.title: Jordi Visser Says One Overlooked Event Could Help Bitcoin Break Out Of Its Slump
data.description:
Key points:
  • Jordi Visser said high real yields, about 250 basis points on the 10-year, have been "a major drag on crypto" and gold this year.
  • He said the Treasury's Nov. 4 refunding could ease that pressure if it trims long-bond sales, a move Citi also expects.
  • He said Bitcoin has tracked semiconductors almost one-for-one and expects a retest of $73,000 to $74,000.

Wall Street veteran Jordi Visser said next week's U.S. Treasury refinancing announcement could ease the pressure on Bitcoin (BTC), gold and artificial intelligence (AI) stocks this year.

Speaking on Anthony Pompliano's podcast on Friday, Visser said high real interest rates have been the main drag on crypto and gold. With inflation expectations around 2.5% and the 10-year yield near 5%, "there's 250 basis points of real 10-year yields," he said.

After the U.S. Treasury said in August that it would double long-term bond buybacks from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation. Bitcoin went up about 21% in just 72 hours.

Why Visser Sees The Refinancing As Catalyst For Bitcoin

Visser pointed to the Treasury's quarterly refunding announcement scheduled for November 4, which will determine how much debt the government will sell and at which maturities. "This is not getting a ton of press," he said. According to Visser, Treasury could cut sales of long-term bonds and shift borrowing to shorter-term debt. "It's not yield curve control, but it is certainly an admission that they don't want the long end to go higher," he added.

Similarly, strategists at Citi, including head of U.S. rates strategy Jason Williams, reportedly expect the Treasury to cut the size of 20-year and 30-year bond auctions by $3 billion each.

Visser also tied the issue to heavy borrowing by AI companies, which compete with the Treasury for investors. He singled out Oracle (ORCL), which raised more than $60 billion since last September. At its investor day this week, Oracle signalled it isn't "going to raise much money between now and June," Visser said.

Muted Moves

Visser said Bitcoin's subdued reaction to the Binance (BNB) hack reflected lower volatility, which has "been lower than AI names all year." He said Bitcoin moved largely in step with semiconductor stocks over the past six weeks. Visser expects Bitcoin to retest $73,000 to $74,000, and possibly dip slightly below.

His comments came as Bitcoin’s price was down by 0.1% during the past 24 hours, trading around $77,500. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

data.title: American Speculators and Prospectors Find It's Hard to Make Money in Greenland — WSJ
data.description:
By Sune Engel Rasmussen

The deal President Trump struck to end his quest to control Greenland has opened the door to a wave of prospectors who are hoping to cash in on riches they believe are locked beneath the ice.

Among them is Texas oil hunter Robert Price, who is betting he can extract up to 13 billion barrels on the Arctic island — roughly on par with the largest oil deposit in North America at Prudhoe Bay, Alaska.

"I've drilled for, and I have found, millions of barrels of oil in my career," Price said. "I've never had an opportunity to drill for billions of barrels."

For at least 150 years, a parade of American speculators and political leaders have been drawn to Greenland — only to have their ambitions thwarted by the stark realities on the ground, both political and geological.

The latest generation of prospectors is betting this time will be different.

They will have to overcome a bevy of obstacles that have complicated such endeavors for decades: locals suspicious of American intentions, efforts to preserve the island's environment and traditional way of life, and one of the harshest physical climates in the world.

Danish and Greenlandic geologists say Price is overestimating both his odds of success and the amount of oil that might be there. There is no more than a 7% chance of finding usable oil anywhere in the basin due to erosion, degradation and other geological risks, they say.

Price, the 66-year-old chief executive of Denver-based Greenland Energy Company, is undeterred. His plans to drill for oil caught the attention of Phil McGraw, a vocal Trump supporter better known as Dr. Phil, who planned a six-part documentary series in which he would accompany "wildcatter" Price and livestream his drilling attempts.

Price isn't alone. Other American investors circling the island include Drew Horn, a former Green Beret who has plans for a hydropowered AI data center, and Josette Sheeran, a former head of the World Food Program, who chairs an investment group called Greenland Development Partners.

Trump hailed the opportunity for Americans this month after signing the deal with Greenland and Denmark that blocks U.S. rivals China and Russia from investing in the island's natural resources without American approval, and eases the international tension around Greenland that has deterred investors. "Massive Oil, Gas and Mineral Exploration is getting ready to begin in our new and beautiful Greenland!" Trump said on Truth Social.

"The U.S. has deepened its foothold," said Mikkel Vedby Rasmussen, political science professor at the University of Copenhagen. "If the U.S. wants to increase its influence in Greenland — which will require some investment — well, then that path is more open than it was before."

Horn is hoping the recent agreement will help lift any lingering suspicions surrounding his efforts. He was among at least three Americans whose visits to the island prompted the Danish government last year to summon the U.S. envoy over accusations that they were working covertly to turn Greenlanders against Denmark, which owns the self-governing territory.

Horn first visited Greenland as a member of a Greenland Policy Coordination Committee, which was formed by the first Trump administration as a body under the National Security Council to explore securing U.S. interests there. He called the allegations that he was part of a covert influence campaign "fantastical."

Horn now heads the GreenMet advisory firm to arrange mineral deals between the U.S. government and private companies. "In reality, I'm just a businessman trying to do deals that benefit all parties. And of course make me and my shareholders the maximum return possible," said Horn.

Sheeran, the former WFP head who served as undersecretary to Condoleezza Rice during her time as secretary of state, is also behind an investment group that has stirred up local questions about its intentions.

Greenland's parliament in Nuuk last year passed a law banning foreigners and nonresidents from buying property on the island. In June, Sheeran's group, Greenland Development Partners, paid $823,000 for a house in central Nuuk in the name of a local business partner, Jørgen Wæver Johansen, according to a bank receipt reviewed by The Wall Street Journal. Sheeran's group previously invested in a local boutique spring-water company that Johansen co-owns, and which until recently appeared dormant, according to Greenland's business registry.

Shortly after the house sale, Sheeran arrived to take measurements for furniture, the house's previous owner said. The purchase of the house was earlier reported by Danish newspaper Weekendavisen.

Greenland Development Partners appears to do little actual business in Greenland. A website in its name advertises various investment opportunities, including in hydropower and a submarine telecom cable. However, the Journal wasn't able to verify the identities of 10 team members and advisers listed on the site. A financial institution listed on the site, Nordic Development Bank, has no digital footprint or records of its existence.

Emails sent to all listed addresses for the investment group bounced back. The only contact number on the site connects with an ordering hotline for Domino's Pizza in Denmark.

Sheeran didn't respond to requests for comment. Johansen didn't respond to questions about why Sheeran's group bought a house in his name.

Price, the Texas oil hunter, encountered a barrage of questions this summer when he swept in by helicopter to inform locals in the village of Ittoqqortoormiit of his plans to drill near their homes. Residents suspected he had ties to Trump, and they worried that drilling would damage the waters and hunting grounds they depend on for survival.

Greenland Energy doesn't hold the rights to drill for oil in Greenland. Those belong to 80 Mile, a British company. Price is paying 80 Mile to drill wells at a two-million-acre site on the Jameson Land peninsula in exchange for gradually taking up to a 70% stake in the licenses.

After Price's contentious meeting in Ittoqqortoormiit, the head of 80 Mile, an Australian prospector named Roderick McIllree, took the reins as managing director of Greenland Energy, in an apparent effort to steady the ship. He called off Dr. Phil's documentary, which had helped prompt rumors the project had ties to Trump.

McIllree, who has operated in Greenland for two decades, said his American partners had gotten carried away. "Anyone who turns up for the first time goes, 'Holy s — , this place is amazing.' Ultimately, they forgot whose house they were in," he said. "You gotta respect the Greenlanders. There's a way to do these things."

A few weeks later, however, Greenland Energy towed a barge with an excavator and containers to the peninsula without the permission of the Greenlandic government, which publicly threatened to send the police and military to deal with "unlawful activities." The company postponed drilling at least until late next year.

Price's oil venture is financed by $90 million raised by Larry Swets, an Illinois-based investor. The money also bought the company access to a second 80 Mile license, to a mineral deposit in west Greenland. Swets said he believes U.S. entrepreneurship can develop Greenland in a way Danish state subsidies — or foreign aggression — haven't.

"I could make money in 10 other ways, probably way easier than this," Swets said. "But the driving force for me was that I believe an American-style capitalism can make an actual difference in a place where everyone else, quite frankly, has done a lot of talking and not a lot of doing."

Swets also chairs a company that seeks to deploy robots to Greenland to enhance local manufacturing. To win local trust, Swets in August delivered a 36-page proposal to the White House, calling for it to end a U.S. ban on seal products, Greenland's export of which has collapsed under international restrictions. Swets called his "sealskin diplomacy" a confidence-building gesture to his Greenlandic friends.

"If that's buying influence, then I guess, aren't our whole lives just buying influence with our friends?" Swets said.

Write to Sune Engel Rasmussen at sune.rasmussen@wsj.com

data.title: Real estate stocks shine in October amid broader tech rout, lower long-term borrowing costs
data.description:
Real estate stocks outperformed the broader markets in October as rotation out of technology stocks benefited the sector, while the Federal Reserve held its rates steady.

The broader AI sector faced a reality check after OpenAI revised its annualized revenue expectations downward, triggering heavy investor scrutiny over the sustainability of massive infrastructure capital expenditures.

The Cboe Volatility Index surged to a four-month high during the month amid circulating market rumors that a major hedge fund had collapsed, reflecting fresh tech struggles.

Persistent technology trade selloff led to major market averages declining in October ahead of the midterm elections.

Meanwhile, President Donald Trump signed an executive order this month that aims to reduce the cost of owning a home. The order directs Bill Pulte, the director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to create a pilot program to cancel borrowers' mortgage insurance premiums proactively once the borrowers have satisfied their equity requirements based on current market value.

Furthermore, long-term borrowing costs decreased during the month. The United States 10-Year Bond Yield fell by 35 basis points to 4.93%. The United States 30-Year Bond Yield reduced by 32 basis points to 5.31%.

The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) increased 4.98% during the month to 275.07 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF was up 5.52% to $43.17.

The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index rose 4.68%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index added 4.58% during the course of the week.

Weekly Winners & Losers

Among largecap stocks, Jones Lang LaSalle led the gainers, advancing 19.81% to $359.79. The real estate services provider reported a third-quarter earnings beat.

Data center REITs Equinix (+6.14% W/W to $1,013.70) and Iron Mountain (+5.99% W/W to $116.55) were gaining ahead of the U.S. midterm elections despite a technology rout this week.

On the election day, voters in 10 U.S. states are set to decide whether to curb data center development in their communities.

Extra Space Storage followed with a 5.52% addition to $151.32, benefitting from financial results that exceeded analyst expectations, while the full-year core FFO guidance was raised.

CoStar Group led the losers in the category. The stock fell 11.06% week-over-week to $30.17 after releasing its Q3 financial results and disclosing a deal to acquire Vexcel for $730M.

Sun Communities lost 5.81% to close the week at $113.26 as Q3 revenue missed analyst estimates.

For the midcap decliners, Compass (-7.69% W/W to $9.00) led the pack.

The stock's price target was lowered at JPMorgan and UBS. Higher mortgage rates and slowing luxury activity reduce near-term earnings visibility for the company, according to UBS.

Alexandria Real Estate Equities followed with a 6.56% pull back to $40.20 despite the company turning in stronger-than-expected Q3 earnings and revenue even as its occupancy rate dipped and same-store net operating income slipped from a year ago.

The life sciences campus landlord refined its guidance for the full-year 2026 adjusted FFO per share to $6.38-$6.42, vs. its previous outlook of $6.35-$6.45.

Cushman & Wakefield led the midcap gainers, adding 12.43% week-over-week to $13.30 ahead of its Q3 earnings release. The company is expected to post an EPS of $0.36 (+22.95% Y/Y) and revenue of $2.79B (+7.11% Y/Y).

For the smallcap stocks, PennyMac Mortgage Investment Trust (+6.11% W/W to $7.47), Chatham Lodging Trust (+5.13% W/W to $14.75), Arbor Realty Trust (-26.71% W/W to $2.14), Farmland Partners (-17.76% W/W to $8.43), and Medical Properties Trust (-16.67% W/W to $2.25) were the notable movers.

data.title: Binance says 90% of stolen assets replenished, targets Sunday withdrawals
data.description:
Binance said Saturday it had replenished 90% of the assets stolen in its $6.3 billion hack, up from about 80% a day earlier.

The cryptocurrency exchange said it remained on track to resume withdrawals Sunday.
